videos.script: Customer number one joined the shop in 2022 as a reader. In January 2024 they became a regular. A year later, a patron. {{customer}} Now the manager asks how much the shop sold to patrons in 2024. {{question}} If the customer table holds only today's tier, every one of that customer's 2024 sales counts as a patron's sale. It was not. {{wrong}} Dimensions describe things, and things change: people move, get promoted, change their names. The question is what the warehouse does when they do. {{change}} There are three classic answers, numbered by Kimball. Type one overwrites, and the past moves with the present. Type two keeps a new row for every version, and each sale points at the version that was true. Type three keeps one previous value beside the current one. {{types}} Ana builds all three on the shop's customers, and asks the same question of each. They give different numbers, and each number is right for a different question. {{build}} Then she loads a month at a time, the way a real warehouse does, and checks the result the way a real warehouse should. {{load}}
